rules: Swapping only the normalizing OHLC field inside a range ratio (rho 0.965, even with a window change too) or only the volume-transform LOG vs TS_RANK inside a ratio denominator (rho 0.981, same window) doesn't decorrelate -- change the numerator's structure, not just what normalizes it.
Downside/upside return-volatility ratios (|t| 0.22) and price-range-vs-volume-delta correlations (|t| 0.18) were this round's weakest cheap_screen misses -- both remain low-probability shapes here.

A 252-day TS_RANK($close) spread failed coverage at exactly 0.874, matching prior 252-day price attempts regardless of the expression wrapped around them -- treat 252 days as a hard coverage ceiling for price windows, not just fundamentals.

The round's two best accepts (fitness 5.470 and 3.867) both crossed a fundamental-or-extremum magnitude leg with a volume-rank or short summed-range normalizer, not two directional/return legs -- keep favoring that magnitude-times-normalizer shape.

A time-series statistic (rank, delta, or dispersion-of-rank) of within-name price momentum on $close or $open, crossed with a time-series rank of dollar volume (windows 42-63), failed the cheap screen three times this round, |t| 0.19-0.42. Pair a price-momentum leg with a cross-sectional fundamental rank instead of a volume rank in this product shape.

5 of 20 rejects (25%) were flagged as duplicates within the same batch, not archive collisions. Two were the same close-minus-low ratio over a 10-day window with only the denominator field swapped; three were earnings-per-share ratio variants (an upside/downside truncation pair, plus a high-minus-low sibling of the accepted open-minus-low version). Check new proposals against the rest of the batch before submitting, not just the archive.

The close-minus-low range divided by a volatility/dispersion term and smoothed over 10 days failed for every denominator tried this round (a dollar-volume volatility term via correlation, a return volatility term and a dollar-volume rank via duplicate). This numerator/window pairing looks exhausted regardless of denominator; change the window or the numerator instead of swapping denominators again.

Earnings-per-share ranked against an intraday price-position ratio was oversampled this round: open-low, high-low, close-open, and close-high variants (bare and time-series-ranked) were all proposed. Only the bare open-low version survived; the high-low version duplicated it and the two time-series-ranked variants correlated at 0.81. Submit at most one such field pairing per batch.

This round's best fitness (6.725) used no fundamental or volume leg at all: a cross-sectional close-versus-high gap crossed with a time-series rank of how far today's high sits below its own 21-day rolling high. This is a subtraction-based distance-from-rolling-extremum, not a ratio; worth trying on other fields (low versus its rolling minimum, close versus its own rolling maximum) and windows.

A range-position ratio mixing a 10-day rolling minimum with a 21-day rolling maximum still correlated at 0.976 with the all-21-day version of the same ratio. Changing only one of two window parameters inside a multi-window ratio does not decorrelate it from the matched-window original.

A 105-day price delta ranked over a 189-day window missed the coverage bar (0.854) even paired with a 90-day dollar-volume leg. Keep combined price-momentum windows (delta length plus the outer rank window) well under that range.

This round's fundamental-times-single-price-rank accepts scored only 0.98-1.37 (return on assets times a close-rank delta, return on equity times an open rank), well below the 2.0-3.6 fitness this template hit in earlier rounds. Treat it as a low-yield refill and prioritize the earnings-magnitude or extremum-distance shapes instead.
